text:
anya: Heads up — our p50 on dedicated-pool-west climbed from 18ms -> 120ms around 09:18. Telemetry shows an increase in PCIe RT latency on rack-42. Anyone watching hardware metrics?

rick: saw that alert. Correlates with nvlink_err counters on node-r42n3 and unusually high PCIe read stalls. `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` shows bursty util every ~90s.

shao: Profiles look like a large data-prep job hammering host->GPU transfers (small buffers, high qps). Could be a model-parallel job using lots of DMA transactions. Tenants impacted are a mix of fractionals and one dedicated analytics customer.

mike: Is this noisy neighbor or a host driver regression? Any recent ubuntu/kernel updates in that AZ?
devops-bot: anomaly-detect: PCIe-rt-latency spike detected on rack-42 at 09:17:36. Affected pods: frac-ml-34, frac-ml-87, dedicated-analytics-2. Auto-tagged: noisy-neighbor-suspect.

anya: No cluster-wide kernel upgrades in the past week. Build pipeline shows one tenant pushed a new binary last night — could be their data loader change.

rick: Can we throttle their egress to test? We have per-tenant egress qdisc but not per-DMA. I can quickly throttle their NIC to see if p50 returns.

shao: Throttling NIC might not affect PCIe bursts if they are host memcpy-heavy. Maybe we should try isolating on-site: move frac-ml-34 to empty warm-pool slot in rack-18 and watch. Migration cost is nontrivial but cheaper than SLA hits.

mike: Can we patch scheduler to prefer rack-local placement for heavy host->GPU patterns? If a tenant is I/O heavy we can push them to nodes with NVLink-rich topology.

anya: Quick experiment: rick, can you cordon r42n3 and migrate frac-ml-34? If latency drops, we confirm noisy tenant. Keep migration to one job only.

rick: On it. `kubectl cordon r42n3` -> draining small job. Moving frac-ml-34 -> rack-18/warm-slot-7. Starting migration at 09:22.

shao: Also toss in `perf record -a -g` on r42n3 for 2 mins to capture host-side DMA bursts.

(09:24) rick: Migration completed. p50 for dedicated-pool-west back to ~22ms. PCIe read stalls dropped ~85%. Looks like frac-ml-34 was the trigger.

anya: Good repro. Next steps: 1) throttle or isolate that tenant in long-term (put into noisy-tenant pool), 2) add eBPF probe for PCIe DMA burst detection, 3) run cost estimate for dedicated noisy-pool.

mike: For (1) we can create a transient dedicated noisy-pool (reserved spare nodes) with soft isolation. Cost: ~0.6x of a full dedicated carve (rough back-of-envelope $3.2k/mo for current usage). I'll add numbers to ticket.

shao: For (2) I can prototype an eBPF kprobe watching dma_map_* calls and count high-rate bursts. If threshold exceeded, trigger placement action. Low effort PoC in 2 days.

devops-bot: incident: created INC-2025-101 for rack-42 PCIe noisy tenant (severity: medium). Assigned: rick.

anya: Owners: rick -> remediation + tenant contact, shao -> eBPF PoC, mike -> cost calc + noisy-pool sizing. We should also notify SRE about potential preemptible churn if we migrate more jobs.

rick: I'll reach out to tenant owner (user: @dataflow) to request they throttle their loader or shift to bulk transfers. Will cc customer success if they want to move to dedicated.

shao: One more note — add a scheduler label `io_pattern=host_mem` that tenants can opt into to avoid noisy co-tenancy. Not default.

mike: Agree. We'll need dashboarding for PCIe-rt-latency by rack and a weekly sweep for noisy patterns. I'll propose budget in infra-planning.

anya: OK locking this thread. Keep INC-2025-101 updated with migration logs, perf captures, and customer outreach. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
